author: Independent Part B recertification auditor (not Workstream D, no reuse of Workstream D's own test file)
mandate: Independently try to FALSIFY Workstream D's claim in docs/phase-3f1-6-rx-final-terminal-closure/06-condition-verification-architecture.json that condition-suspicion.ts's slot-grammar frames are genuinely compositional/generalized rather than a closed enumerated list dressed up in different variable names, using FRESH adversarial condition formulations never seen by that remediation's own development or test suite.

priorArtifactReviewed.productionCode: lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic-verification/condition-suspicion.ts (read in full, all 9 pattern categories) and lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic-verification/source-inventory.ts (read in full, confirmed CONDITION_SUSPICION_PATTERNS is spread into PATTERNS unchanged)
existingTestFileCheckedForOverlap: tests/contract-model/condition-suspicion-architecture.test.ts (Workstream D's own 34-test file - 12 required-class cases + 2 novel-combination cases + benign/precision + false-positive guards)
priorArtifactReviewed.overlapFindings: None of the 7 fresh constructions used below (subjunctive 'should X occur' inversion x2, light-noun 'circumstance', trigger-preposition synonyms 'subsequent to' and bare 'on', cross-reference connective synonym 'as referenced in', and 'insofar as') appear as literal text, or as a named required class, in any of the above files. They were chosen specifically to sit just outside each frame's own enumerated closed word-list while remaining ordinary, realistic credit-agreement/commercial-contract drafting.

codeVerifiedAssessment.question: Is condition-suspicion.ts genuinely compositional/generalized, or does it still bottom out in a closed enumerated list dressed up in different variable names?
codeVerifiedAssessment.answer: STILL FUNDAMENTALLY A FINITE ENUMERATED-LIST ARCHITECTURE, JUST WITH THE ENUMERATION MOVED DOWN ONE LEVEL FROM 'WHOLE PHRASE' TO 'CONNECTIVE/PREPOSITION/PARTICIPLE WORD, PLUS A HARD-CODED SLOT SHAPE.' The design doc's own honestSelfAssessment already disclosed this in the abstract ('the connective/preposition/participle/light-noun VOCABULARY in every frame is still a finite, hand-written set... a sufficiently exotic, never-anticipated connective... could still slip through'). This recertification confirms, with real running code, that the disclosed limitation is not a hypothetical edge case - it is trivially and repeatedly reachable with ordinary, non-exotic legal English that a real drafter would write on any given day, including several forms that are arguably MORE common in real credit agreements than some of the 12 forms the remediation's own test matrix does cover (e.g. the subjunctive 'Should X occur' conditional inversion, which appears at least as frequently in real credit agreements as 'in the event that').
keyCodeLevelFindings: Every one of the 9 categories keys its detection on a small, closed, HAND-TYPED alternation of specific English words (prepositions: upon|following|after|before|once; light nouns: event|case, extent|degree; occurrence verbs: occurred|arisen|taken place; satisfaction participles: deemed|satisfied|fulfilled|met|achieved|complied with|eligible|entitled|qualified; modals: shall|will|is|are|has been|have been; citation connectives: in accordance with|pursuant to|as set forth...|set forth...). None of these closed lists is exhaustive of the real English words that perform the identical grammatical/semantic function, and the module has no mechanism (morphological, syntactic, or otherwise) for recognizing an unlisted synonym performing the same role - it is a literal regex alternation, not a generalized grammar.

DIRECT DOCUMENT/CODE MISMATCH FOUND: the design doc's own honestSelfAssessment.whatGenuinelyGeneralizes text, and condition-suspicion.ts's own Category 2 doc comment, both explicitly state the NOMINAL_CONDITIONAL_CONNECTIVE light-noun slot is 'event/case/circumstance/extent/degree'. The actual shipped regex (NOMINAL_CONDITIONAL_CONNECTIVE_RE) is `/\b(?:in\s+the\s+(?:event|case)\s+(?:of|that|where)|to\s+the\s+(?:extent|degree)\s+(?:that|to\s+which)|in\s+case\s+(?:of|that)|on\s+condition\s+that)\b/gi` - it contains only 'event' and 'case', never 'circumstance'. The document's own self-assessment overclaims the breadth of its own shipped code. Verified directly by extracting and printing the live regex source in a new test (see testFile.codeLevelTest below) - 'circumstance' is provably absent from the pattern the document claims contains it.

The EVENT_TRIGGER_NOMINALIZATION frame's genuinely open part (the morphological suffix class on the noun) is real and does generalize as claimed - but it is gated behind a closed 5-word preposition list (upon|following|after|before|once). An otherwise-perfect nominalization match ('the occurrence of X') is silently dropped entirely if the preceding trigger word is any ordinary synonym outside that list ('on', 'subsequent to', 'in the wake of', 'consequent upon', 'immediately on'), because the whole frame is a single concatenated regex requiring the preposition token adjacent to the noun.

The subjunctive-inversion conditional ('Should X occur, ...', 'Were the Company to breach..., ...') - one of the two or three most common conditional sentence forms in English generally, and specifically common in credit-agreement drafting as a stylistic variant of 'If X occurs' - is not modeled by ANY of the 9 categories, not even partially. It is not a nominalization, not a trigger-preposition-plus-defined-term, not a perfect-aspect occurrence predicate (it uses the bare subjunctive base form 'occur', not 'has/have ... occurred'), and not a modal-satisfaction passive. This is a gap in the grammar coverage itself, not merely an unlisted synonym within an existing frame - i.e. it is evidence the remediation's own category list, while broader than a flat phrase list, was still built by enumerating the SPECIFIC 12 required test classes rather than by a principled grammar of English conditionals.

CROSS_REFERENCE_INCORPORATION's citation-connective slot generalizes over the citation identifier (confirmed genuine, per the design doc) but not over the connective phrase itself - 'as referenced in Schedule X', 'as described in Exhibit Y', 'per Section Z' are all ordinary synonyms for the modeled 'as set forth in'/'pursuant to'/'in accordance with' set and are not detected.
codeVerifiedAssessment.conclusionOnArchitectureClaim: The remediation is a genuine, disclosed improvement over a flat single-idiom list (it correctly closes the 8 specific Part B gaps and the 12 specific required test classes, and two of its slot dimensions - the nominalization suffix and the citation identifier - are authentically open-ended). But it does NOT meet the phase's own stated bar of detecting 'the underlying GRAMMATICAL CONSTRUCTION... regardless of which exact idiom the drafter chose' for constructions outside its 9 named categories or outside each category's own closed connective/participle/preposition vocabulary. It is curve-fit to the specific 12 semantic classes and their component vocabulary that this phase's own charter enumerated as required test classes - not a generalized parse of English conditional grammar. A fifth (or more) recurrence of this exact defect class, with a fifth fresh vocabulary, is mechanically inevitable under the current architecture; the only change from the prior three recurrences is that the next patch would likely be phrased as a 10th 'category' rather than a phrase-list entry, which is a smaller, but not architecturally different, unit of enumeration.

dispositionRationale: The condition-verification architecture delivered by Workstream D under FINDING-5 is a genuine, disclosed improvement over the prior flat CONDITIONAL_PHRASE idiom list - it correctly closes the specific 8 Part B gaps and 12 required semantic-test classes, and two of its slot dimensions (the nominalization suffix class, the cross-reference citation identifier) do generalize as claimed. However, it does NOT satisfy the phase's own non-negotiable architecture rule that condition detection operate on 'generalized compositional structural evidence... never an enumerated phrase list.' Every one of the 9 detection categories is still gated by a small, closed, hand-typed word list at the connective/preposition/participle/modal level, and this recertification demonstrates with real, running production code (not merely by citing the design document's own disclosed limitation) that ordinary, realistic legal drafting - a subjunctive 'Should X occur' inversion, an unlisted light noun ('circumstance', which the design document itself incorrectly claims IS covered), an unlisted trigger preposition ('subsequent to', bare 'on'), and an unlisted cross-reference connective ('as referenced in') - reaches the exact original BLOCKER-9 failure signature: a rule with its qualifying condition completely and silently dropped nonetheless reaches VERIFIED_NO_MATERIAL_GAP_FOUND with semanticReviewInvoked=false, with zero scrutiny from either the deterministic layer or the independent Layer-2 semantic reviewer. Per this phase's own explicit rule, 'a fourth phrase-list patch is an explicit failure of this phase regardless of test pass rate' - this recertification's own-code-verified finding is that the delivered architecture, despite real and disclosed improvement, remains an enumerated-list architecture at a finer grain, and the same defect class should be expected to recur a fifth time with a fifth fresh vocabulary unless the detection mechanism is changed from closed-list regex alternations to something that can recognize a syntactic/semantic ROLE (conditional-clause subordination, event-trigger argument, citation dependency) independent of which specific closed-class word instantiates it.
reproductionEvidence: See testFile.realOutputCapturedVerbatim above for the full per-case reproduction (7 constructions, 14 failing assertions, one direct doc/code word-list mismatch), and tests/contract-model/part-b-recert-finding5-independent.test.ts for the runnable adversarial test file itself.
recommendationForAnyFutureRemediation: Not authorized or attempted by this recertification (production code is frozen for this task) - noted for the record only: the closed word-lists inside each frame (trigger prepositions, light nouns, satisfaction participles, citation connectives) would need to become open-ended (e.g. driven by a real syntactic dependency parse recognizing subordinate-clause/complement structure, or a much larger lexical-semantic class lookup) rather than hand-typed regex alternations, for the architecture to meet its own stated 'detect the construction, not the phrase' bar rather than merely enumerating a longer and finer-grained list of phrases.
